note: Simulation seed for the headless economy prototype. Everything here is a PLACEHOLDER ASSUMPTION used to make existing world data run; values marked (assumed) are not yet canon and are the first things calibration will change. No world file names a filter producer, so the producer and distributor below are assumed. Procurement policy: reorder_point and target_stock in the facility items are FLOORS; companies raise them to cover estimated lead time plus safety_days of planning demand (the larger of consumption and the outflow they supply to others). STOCK-OUT TUNING (2026-10-03): Chandlers safety stock 40->100 so the distributor does not sell its own cover to downstream orders; base rate re-set to 63 after procurement changes (more orders in flight) moved fleet margin. FLEET (2026-10-03): sol_transit_a and redline_coop_a removed (they lost money every run: the slice has far more hulls than freight). npc_board_delay_hours 12 keeps new freight on the board for half a day before AI fleets look at it, so the player gets a real choice. Fleet margin swings by 10+ points between nearby settings because carriers compete for the same lots; treat single runs as noisy. Three frontier export chains give each frontier port outbound freight, from the world data's own export lists: Talos Ore Works sells rare minerals to Meridian Smelter Guild; Waystation Fuel Depot sells fuel to Meridian Bunkering Company; Lastlight Survey Mining Co-op sells platinum-group metals to Roosevelt Instrument Works. All six facilities are assumed. Fleet is 12 carriers (one more Concord Interstellar ship than before the brine chain). Stale freight (sitting more than 8 days) escalates faster and past the normal cap so stranded parcels eventually move. KNOWN SPACE: tools/gen_known_space.py adds a maker and users for every freight good (data/runtime/goods_roles.json) and the carriers to move them. Do not hand-edit the generated entries (ids ending _works, _exchange and the pool carriers); change the roles or the fleet file and regenerate.
